section.title: Introduction
section.p: A verb tells us what happens or what someone does.
Verbs can be derived from other word classes or from other verbs, e.g. ?? and ??. Read more about verb derivation.
Verbs have both finite and non-finite forms:

ul.li: Non-finite forms do not express person or number, e.g. the infinitive xxx (to come) and the past participle xxx (come).
Finite forms express mood, person and number.

section.p: Mood expresses the speaker's attitude towards what is said. Skolt Sámi has four moods:
Person and number are inflectional categories expressing agreement with the subject: xxx 'xxx', xxx 'xxx' (I 'come', we 'come', she 'comes', we 'come').
When inflecting verbs, pay attention to vowel and consonant alternations and palatalisation.
